slot.brief: Coulomb-force analogy question: two protons repel with a given force; ask for force at a new separation or force between alpha particles at the same separation.

stem: Two protons separated by a distance $r$ repel with a force of $3.0\times10^{-8}$ N. What is the repulsive force between two $\alpha$ particles separated by the same distance?

verdicts.working: By Coulomb’s law, force scales with the product of the charges. Each alpha particle has charge +2e, so the force is 4 times as large: 4(3.0×10⁻⁸ N) = 1.2×10⁻⁷ N.

working:
$F\propto q_1q_2$ at fixed separation.\nEach alpha particle has charge $2e$, so $F_{\alpha\alpha}=\dfrac{(2e)(2e)}{e^2}F_{pp}=4(3.0\times10^{-8})=1.2\times10^{-7}$ N.

Independent check: By Coulomb’s law, force scales with the product of the charges. Each alpha particle has charge +2e, so the force is 4 times as large: 4(3.0×10⁻⁸ N) = 1.2×10⁻⁷ N.
solution:
By Coulomb’s law, at fixed separation $F\propto q_1q_2$. Each $\alpha$ particle has charge $+2e$, so
$$F_{\alpha\alpha}=4F_{pp}=4(3.0\times10^{-8})=1.2\times10^{-7}\,\text{N}.$$
